skill.displayName: 门诊收费与退费日结核对（免费版）

llm.summary: The skill appears to perform a local cashier reconciliation check, but its documentation gives conflicting network/privacy claims and describes host/user-derived usage tracking that is not implemented in the inspected code.

dimensions.detail: Read and Bash access are proportionate for running the bundled Node script against a user-selected input file, but the workflow may involve sensitive hospital cashier and refund data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package manager step, dependency download, or remote payload retrieval was found; the referenced local scripts are present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill prominently claims no network access, but later documentation and script help text describe anonymous server-side run counting, a host/user-derived identifier, and a --no-stats option that the inspected script does not parse or implement.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No file writes, persistence hooks, or implemented telemetry were found, but the documentation describes a persistent anonymous installation identifier derived from hostname and username, which is unnecessary for the local checking purpose.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core capability is coherent: a Node.js script reads a user-supplied reconciliation table and performs deterministic local arithmetic, duplicate, blank, and negative-amount checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the documentation inconsistency. The inspected version appears local and does not implement telemetry, but the published text says it may contact a server and derive an anonymous identifier from hostname and username. Use it on exported copies of records rather than live systems, and verify future versions before use if offline operation matters.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted as a documentation and user-expectation concern: early metadata says no network, while later text describes server-side usage statistics. The inspected code does not actually perform the network behavior.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: the artifact is inconsistent about being completely local. This supports Review, but not maliciousness, because no fetch/http/net/dns/tls usage or data upload code was found.
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: scripts/run.mjs and the engine file are present and were fully inspected locally; the reference is an expected usage command, not evidence of evasion.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted as a stated-design concern because host/user-derived run-count identifiers are not needed for local reconciliation. However, this behavior appears documented but not implemented in the inspected script.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted as an under-disclosure concern for SKILL.md: the command examples appear before the later usage-statistics section, although script help text does mention stats.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-only instructions and output align with the Chinese-language hospital reconciliation workflow and are not a security concern by themselves.
